learn.title: App Service, Azure Functions and serverless hosting
objectives: Describe Azure App Service and App Service plans.
Use App Service features: deployment slots, autoscale, custom domains, authentication and WebJobs.
Describe Azure Functions hosting plans, triggers and bindings.
Describe Azure Logic Apps for low-code serverless workflows.
Choose between App Service, Functions, Logic Apps, containers and VMs for a workload.
concepts: Azure App Service
A fully managed PaaS for hosting web apps, REST APIs and mobile back ends on Windows or Linux. It supports .NET, Java, Node.js, Python and PHP, and custom containers.
App Service plan
Defines the region, tier, VM size and instance count that your apps run on. You pay for the plan, and all apps in a plan share its instances.
Deployment slots
Separate live environments, such as staging, with their own hostnames. Swap a slot into production for near-zero-downtime releases. Available on Standard tier and higher.
Autoscale
Rules that add or remove App Service plan instances based on metrics or a schedule. Available on Standard tier and higher.
WebJobs
Background tasks that run in the same context as an App Service app.
Function app
The unit that hosts one or more functions. Its functions share a hosting plan, scaling and settings.
Triggers and bindings
Each function has exactly one trigger (HTTP, timer, queue, Event Hubs, Service Bus, Cosmos DB and so on) and any number of input and output bindings.
Functions hosting plans
Consumption (pay per execution, scales to zero), Flex Consumption, Premium (pre-warmed instances, virtual network integration) and Dedicated (runs on an App Service plan).
Azure Logic Apps
A designer-first serverless workflow service with connectors. Consumption logic apps are multitenant and billed per run; Standard logic apps are single-tenant and can host several workflows.
Azure Static Web Apps
Hosting for static front ends (for example React or Angular) with integrated serverless APIs.
comparisons: App Service: always-on web apps and APIs, billed per plan. Functions: event-driven code, billed per execution on Consumption.
Functions: code-first. Logic Apps: designer-first workflows with connectors.
App Service: the platform manages the OS and web server. VMs: full OS control, and you patch it.
ACI vs Container Apps vs AKS
ACI: a single container, simplest. Container Apps: serverless microservices that scale to zero. AKS: full managed Kubernetes.
traps: A stopped app, or an empty App Service plan, still costs money. You pay for the plan.
Deploying to a staging slot doesn't make it live. You must swap.
Free and Shared tiers run on infrastructure shared with other customers, and Free doesn't support custom domains.
Consumption-plan functions have a maximum timeout of 10 minutes (default 5).
Windows and Linux apps can't share the same App Service plan.
revision: App Service = PaaS web hosting; the plan sets price and capacity.
Slots and autoscale need Standard tier or higher. Isolated tier = App Service Environment.
One trigger per function; bindings connect to data without extra code.
Consumption = per execution and scales to zero. Premium = no cold start and virtual network access. Dedicated = App Service plan.
Logic Apps = visual workflows with connectors, and the on-premises data gateway for local systems.
Pick: website → App Service; events → Functions; workflow → Logic Apps; single container → ACI; orchestration → AKS; full OS control → VM.
